title: A Day on the Beach
cardDescription: Take a seaside break with familiar words for sand, shoreline features, and things brought on a beach visit.
description: Take a seaside break with familiar words for sand, shoreline features, and things brought on a beach visit.
focus: The clues mix natural beach features with ordinary objects used during a visit. Some answers name a place or a surface; others name a belonging.
solvingTip: Check whether a clue describes the setting or something carried on a visit. Small familiar objects can help cross longer shoreline words.
words: Sandy or pebbly land beside a sea or lake
Loose small grains covering many beaches
Mound of windblown sand near a shore
Absorbent cloth spread on sand or used for drying
Handled container used to carry beach sand
Small digging tool used to build a sandcastle
Portable canopy used to make shade on a beach
Star that lights a clear day at the beach
Head covering worn on a beach outing
Portable seat set up beside the shore
Meal packed to be eaten outdoors
Woven container that may hold an outdoor meal
Insulated box used to carry chilled food or drinks
Land along the edge of a large body of water
Small rounded stone found on some beaches
Mark left by a bare foot in damp sand
To travel on foot along the beach
To take a quiet break from activity
Large cloth spread out for sitting on the sand

answerNotes.DUNE: A dune is formed from sand moved by wind. It names a landform rather than an object carried to the beach.
answerNotes.SPADE: Spade names a digging tool here. The same word also names one suit in a deck of cards.
answerNotes.COOLER: Cooler is the American word for an insulated carrying box. The clue asks for the container rather than a comparative temperature.
answerNotes.SHORE: Shore is the land beside a body of water. Beach describes a sandy or pebbly part of that boundary.
answerNotes.PEBBLE: A pebble is a small stone. The clue emphasizes its rounded form rather than the loose grains called sand.
answerNotes.FOOTPRINT: A footprint is an impression left behind. It names the mark rather than the foot that made it.

title: Waves and Changing Tides
cardDescription: Follow the shoreline through words for waves, tides, and the places where water meets land.
description: Follow the shoreline through words for waves, tides, and the places where water meets land.
focus: This puzzle describes moving seawater and familiar coastal features. Clues distinguish parts of a wave, changes in water level, and solid structures along a shore.
solvingTip: Look for whether a clue asks for a wave part, a tidal movement, or a coastal feature. Opposite movement words and short water terms can provide useful crossings.
words: Moving ridge of water that may break near a shore
Regular rise and fall of sea level
Describing the tide when the sea reaches its upper level
Describing the tide at its lower level
Earth's natural satellite whose gravity strongly influences tides
Flow of seawater in a particular direction
Long rolling wave that may travel far from a storm
Small wave or undulation on water
Mass of bubbles left by breaking waves
Low area between two wave crests
To recede, as tidal water when its level falls
To move as a liquid in a steady stream
Ridge of sand formed in shallow water
Ridge of rock or coral at or near the sea's surface
Solid stone exposed along a rugged coast
Structure projecting from shore into water
Small body of water left among coastal rocks

answerNotes.TIDE: Tides describe recurring sea-level changes. They differ from individual waves moving across the water's surface.
answerNotes.MOON: The Moon's gravity is a major influence on tides. The Sun also contributes, so the Moon is not the only influence.
answerNotes.SWELL: Swell consists of rolling waves that can travel beyond the place where wind generated them. It is a wave term rather than a tidal level.
answerNotes.CREST: The crest is the wave's top. The trough is the lower area between crests, so position distinguishes the words.
answerNotes.EBB: Ebb describes the falling or outgoing tide. The word names a movement rather than a structure on the shore.
answerNotes.SANDBAR: A sandbar is a ridge built from deposited sand. A reef may instead be rock or coral.

title: Shells Along the Shore
cardDescription: Look closely at familiar shell names, curved shapes, and the parts that join a two-piece shell.
description: Look closely at familiar shell names, curved shapes, and the parts that join a two-piece shell.
focus: The clues name shell-bearing animals and visible shell features. Some answers describe a shape or surface; others name a whole animal or a shell part. Direct descriptions introduce the less familiar terms.
solvingTip: Check whether the clue asks for an animal, a shell part, or a surface description. A spiral shell and a shell made of two joined halves have different structures.
words: Hard outer covering made by many mollusks
Burrowing mollusk with a shell made of two joined halves
Irregular-shelled mollusk, some kinds of which produce pearls
Two-shelled mollusk often attached to rocks by strong threads
Mollusk known for a fan-shaped shell with radiating ribs
Marine snail with a spiral shell, often pointed at one end
Large marine snail associated with a heavy spiral shell
Mollusk commonly associated with one coiled shell
Rounded object formed inside certain shelled mollusks
Raised line running along a shell's surface
Curve that winds around a center and gradually expands
One of the two shell halves of a clam
Joint area where two shell halves meet
Having a surface without obvious bumps or ridges
Having an uneven textured shell surface
Raised band radiating across a scallop shell
One complete turn in a coiled shell
Marine mollusk with a low cap-shaped shell
A winding loop in a spiral shell

answerNotes.VALVE: Valve names one half of a two-part mollusk shell. It is a shell structure here rather than a device controlling liquid flow.
answerNotes.HINGE: The hinge connects shell halves at one side. It differs from the free edges that can open apart.
answerNotes.SCALLOP: A scallop shell is often recognized by its fan shape and radiating ribs. The clue uses those visible features.
answerNotes.WHORL: A whorl is one turn in a coiled structure. The full spiral may contain several whorls.
answerNotes.LIMPET: A limpet has a caplike shell. That outline contrasts with the coiled form associated with many other marine snails.
answerNotes.PEARL: Pearls can form inside certain mollusks. The clue does not imply that every oyster or every shell contains one.

title: Around a Small Harbor
cardDescription: Visit a small harbor through familiar words for boats, their parts, and the objects along a dock.
description: Visit a small harbor through familiar words for boats, their parts, and the objects along a dock.
focus: This puzzle follows the objects seen where boats gather. Clues describe locations, vessel parts, and simple equipment by their jobs rather than giving sailing instructions.
solvingTip: Notice whether the clue names part of a boat, a place beside it, or something used to secure it. The rear, upper surface, and main body have distinct names.
words: Sheltered area of water where boats may anchor
Structure beside which a boat can be secured
Platform extending over water on supporting posts
Floating marker anchored in the water
Heavy device lowered to hold a boat in place
Strong thick cord used aboard a boat
Fastening made by tying cord or rope
Upper surface on which people stand aboard a vessel
Large fabric surface that catches wind to move a boat
Long implement used to row a boat
To move a boat with oars
Boat carrying passengers or vehicles across water
Small powerful boat used to move larger vessels
Small light boat often used for rowing
Assigned narrow space where a boat is berthed

answerNotes.BOW: Bow names the front of a vessel and rhymes with cow here. The looped ribbon knot has the same spelling but a different pronunciation.
answerNotes.STERN: Stern is the rear of a boat. The word can also describe a serious manner, but the vessel location determines this meaning.
answerNotes.BUOY: A buoy is a floating marker held in a position by an anchor or mooring. It differs from the fixed platform of a pier.
answerNotes.HULL: The hull is the boat's main body. Deck names an upper surface rather than the whole outer structure.
answerNotes.SLIP: Slip is a berth or assigned boat space in this harbor context. It does not describe losing one's footing.
answerNotes.TUG: Tug names a compact working boat here. Its job distinguishes it from a passenger ferry.

title: Birds Beside the Sea
cardDescription: Meet coastal birds through their recognizable shapes, body parts, and ways of moving near the water.
description: Meet coastal birds through their recognizable shapes, body parts, and ways of moving near the water.
focus: The clues combine bird names with familiar actions and visible features. Descriptions use shape and behavior rather than requiring a particular coast, season, or plumage color.
solvingTip: Ask whether a clue names a bird, a body part, a group, or an action. Short movement words can help cross the longer coastal bird names.
words: Seabird often seen calling and gliding near a harbor
Slender seabird often recognized by pointed wings and a forked tail
Large water bird with a pouch beneath its bill
Stocky seabird known for a colorful bill during breeding season
Dark water bird often seen drying its spread wings
Small shorebird often seen running and pausing on open beaches
Shorebird with a slender bill often probing wet sand
Fish-catching bird of prey that may nest near a coast
Long-legged water bird that often waits motionless for prey
Slender heron often associated with white plumage
Bird's hard mouthpart, rhyming with peak
Spoon___: bird name ending with a word for its mouthpart
Body part a seabird extends while gliding
One lightweight structure covering a coastal bird
Structure where a coastal bird lays eggs
Group of birds gathered or traveling together
To plunge below the water's surface in pursuit of food
To fly high with little visible wing flapping
To move through the air without actively beating the wings

answerNotes.PELICAN: A pelican's pouch hangs beneath its bill. That feature is a more specific clue than size or coastal location alone.
answerNotes.PUFFIN: Puffin bills can look especially colorful in breeding season. Their appearance changes, so the clue specifies that context.
answerNotes.CORMORANT: Cormorants are familiar for a spread-wing posture after swimming. The clue uses a visible behavior rather than a particular species name.
answerNotes.OSPREY: An osprey is a fish-catching bird of prey. It differs from the long-legged birds that hunt by standing in shallow water.
answerNotes.FLOCK: Flock names a group of birds. It is a collective word rather than the name of one species.
answerNotes.WADE: Wade means move on foot through shallow water. Dive describes going beneath the surface instead.
